newsitem.title: USA: Boston Ballet dancer dies, eating disorder blamed.
newsitem.headline: Boston Ballet dancer dies, eating disorder blamed.

text.p: A 22-year-old Boston Ballet dancer died of cardiac arrest, possibly brought on by an eating disorder, after ballet officials told her over a two-year period to lose and then gain weight, the dance company said on Thursday.
Heidi Guenther, one of the 25-member Corps de Ballet, the third tier beneath the ballet's nine principal stars, died while travelling with her family to Disneyland last week.
Ballet spokeswoman Nina Berger said Guenther's friends and some members of her family believed an eating disorder precipitated the dancer's death, although that had not been medically confirmed.
Guenther, a native of Los Osos, California, near San Francisco, weighed 100 pounds (45 kg) and was 5-foot-3-inches (160 cm) tall, Berger said, adding, "That's thin, but not that thin for a dancer."

The ballet's new artistic director, Anna-Marie Holmes, had told the dancer to lose 5 pounds (2 kg) two years ago when she was a member of the Boston Ballet II, the ballet's junior company, Berger said.
Both Guenther's mother and the ballet company had been worried about the dancer's weight loss and she was told she should try to gain some weight.
The San Luis Obispo County, California, coroner was still conducting autopsy tests.
